description: scripts/ci_bookkeeping_gate.py decides, as the first step of every CI job, whether a push to a pull request may skip the job. For a mechanical 'Merge remote-tracking branch origin/main' push it compares the previous head with the new head (2-dot), which sweeps in every file that main changed since the branch point (500+ files, 200+ non-bookkeeping), so the gate answers non-bookkeeping-change and all seven workflows run in full (7 to 9 minutes each) although the pull request's own diff against main is unchanged and main already ran CI on the merged-in commit. Measured on pull requests 295 to 305 of the target repository: 11 such pushes, 7.07 to 9.17 minutes each, about 90 minutes of CI wall time in one hour of queue.
goal: Add a new rule, in a new module scripts/ci_merge_push_gate.py called from decide() in scripts/ci_bookkeeping_gate.py, so a synchronize push whose new head is a clean merge of the base branch into the previous head skips the job only on positive evidence: (1) the new head has exactly two parents and the first is the previous head; (2) the same job really succeeded on the previous head (the existing chain rules) and on the merged-in base commit (a main push run of the same job); (3) the merge is clean: no file in the merge result differs from what git would produce from the two parents, i.e. no conflict-resolution edit; (4) the files changed on the base side since the previous head's merge base and the files the pull request itself changed are disjoint by path and by their parent directory, and no file the pull request changed under apps/ or scripts/ is imported by or tests a file the base side changed in the same top-level directory. Anything else, any API error and any doubt runs the full job exactly as today. The hygiene job keeps running in full (merge markers, Prettier, JSONL). The rule's decision name and detail appear on the gate's one output line.
rationale: Mechanical main-merge pushes are the largest remaining source of repeated full CI runs in a queue of pull requests; positive-evidence skipping keeps the safety property of the existing gate.
acceptance_criteria: A clean two-parent main merge with disjoint changed-file sets, a real success on the previous head and a real success of the same job on the merged-in main commit decides skip with a named rule.

Each of these runs the full job, with its own test: a merge with conflict-resolution edits; overlapping or same-directory changed files; no recorded success on the previous head; no recorded success on the merged-in main commit; a non-merge push; a three-parent merge; the first parent not the previous head; an API error or truncated compare.
Existing bookkeeping-only and label rules and their tests behave exactly as before.
The gate stays standard library only and Python 3.9 syntax; hygiene is never skipped by the new rule.
No file outside the scope list changes; the module budgets file and every budget-check script are untouched.
